references.text: Abraham's lifespan and death: he died at a good old age, old and full of years, and was gathered to his people. This is the direct fulfillment of the promise in 15:15.
Isaac breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. The same wording as in the promise to Abraham, showing that the pattern repeats in the lives of the patriarchs.
Jacob asks Joseph to swear that he will be buried with his ancestors, reflecting the desire to be gathered to his fathers, in line with the promise in 15:15.
Jacob gives instructions for his burial and wishes to be laid with his ancestors in the cave of Machpelah. He was gathered to his people, mirroring the promise to Abraham.

In faith all these died without receiving what was promised, but they saw it from afar and welcomed it, confessing that they were strangers and foreigners on earth. This offers a perspective of faith on the death of the patriarchs and their expectation.
Direct linguistic and theological parallel: The promise to be gathered to one's fathers and to die in peace.
